opportunities.title: fix(api): map Multer upload parser errors to 400
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `POST /api/uploads` uses `upload.single("file")`. When a client sends malformed multipart input such as a file under an unexpected field name (`avatar` instead of `file`), Multer raises a `MulterError` with code `LIMIT_UNEXPECTED_FILE`. The current global error handler treats every such parser error as an unexpected server failure and returns HTTP 500. Malformed multipart input is a client error, so returning 500 is misleading and encourages incorrect retries. ## Expected fix - Recognize Multer parser errors in the shared API error handler. - Return HTTP 400 using the existing `{ success: false, message }` response shape. - Preserve the existing 500 behavior for unrelated unexpected errors. - Add focused regression coverage for an unexpected multipart file field. ## Scope Keep this limited to Multer parser error handling and focused API tests. Do not add file-size policy, MIME filtering, upload authentication, or missing-file handling in this issue. This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50

opportunities.title: [ABI/stdlib] External bool decoder accepts non-canonical returndata: any >=32-byte buffer with leading true-word decodes as true, tail ignored (v26.1.0, v26.2.0)
opportunities.summary: ## Summary The msg-decode helper emitted by fe/Sonatina for external calls returning `bool` accepts **any returndata buffer of at least 32 bytes whose first 32-byte word equals the canonical true word** — everything past byte 32 is silently ignored. A contract author's mental model ("the external call returned exactly one ABI-encoded bool") does not match emitted behavior ("first word is 1, tail is irrelevant"). A counterparty returning `(true, <attacker-controlled data>)` tuples, padded buffers, or stale-memory tails decodes as a clean `true`.
